words.def: To take something or someone with you to a place.
words.note: Say Take this file to the office (away from here), not Bring this file to the office. Bring = toward you or the listener, take = away from you. In Darija جيب is used for both.

ex.en: Can you *bring* some water, please?
ex.ar: واش تقدر تجيب شوية د الما، عافاك؟

ex.en: She *brought* her laptop to the meeting.

col.en: Don't forget to *bring* your ID with you.
You can *bring* a friend along if you want.
I didn't want to *bring* it up in the meeting.
Can you *bring* my charger back tomorrow?

words.def: Very close to something, but not completely.
words.note: Say almost everyone, not almost of the people. Almost goes directly before the word, with no "of".

ex.en: It's *almost* midnight. I need to sleep.
We're *almost* there.

col.en: *Almost* everyone in my class has a laptop.
I *almost* always take the bus to work.
Wait a minute, I'm *almost* ready.
I *almost* forgot your birthday!

words.def: To enjoy yourself and have a good time.
words.note: Say have fun, not make fun. Make fun of someone means to laugh at them in a mean way.

ex.en: I hope you *have fun* on your trip.
We *had fun* at the beach yesterday.

col.en: *Have fun* at the party!
Did you *have fun* at the wedding?
We *had fun* playing football on the beach.
The kids *have fun* with their cousins.

words.def: At the back of something; later or slower than planned.
words.note: Say behind the house, not behind of the house. Don't add "of" after behind.

ex.en: The cat is hiding *behind* the sofa.
Our team is two points *behind*.
ex.ar: الفريق ديالنا متأخر ب جوج نقط.

col.en: Your jacket is *behind* the door.
We're *behind* schedule on this project.
Don't fall *behind* with your homework.
I left my phone *behind* at the office.

words.def: To go to a new place or position; to change where you live.
words.note: Say move to Rabat, not move in Rabat. In Darija we say تنقل ل / ف, but in English use to for the new place.

ex.en: Please *move* a little. I can't see the screen.
ex.ar: عافاك زحزح شوية. ما كنشوفش الشاشة.

ex.en: They want to *move* to Spain.

col.en: We *moved* to Casablanca last year.
My brother *moved* out last month.
Let's *move* on to the next question.
Can you *move* your car, please?

words.def: To see or get something you were looking for; to discover something.
words.note: Say I found it difficult to understand, not I found difficult to understand. You need "it" after find. The past form is found, not finded.

ex.en: I can't *find* my keys.
Did you *find* the answer?

col.en: I'll *find* out and call you back.

col.p_ar: كيلقاها صعيبة باش يدير شي حاجة
col.en: I *find* it hard to speak English on the phone.
It's not easy to *find* a job here.

col.p_ar: يلقى الوقت باش يدير شي حاجة
col.en: I can't *find* time to study this week.

words.note: Say people are, not people is. Also say a lot of people, not a lot of peoples. People is already plural.

ex.en: The *people* in my neighborhood are very kind.
How many *people* are coming to the party?
ex.ar: شحال د الناس غادي يجيو للحفلة؟

col.en: *People* say it's going to rain tomorrow.
A lot of *people* use this app.
Most *people* start work at nine.
Young *people* spend a lot of time on their phones.

words.def: To do something wrong without wanting to.
words.note: Say make a mistake, not do a mistake. In Darija we say دار غلطة (do), but English uses make.

ex.en: I *made a mistake* and sent the email to the wrong person.
Be careful, or you'll *make a mistake*.

col.en: Everyone *makes a mistake* sometimes.
Don't be afraid to *make mistakes* when you speak English.
I *made a mistake* in the email.
Sorry, my *mistake*! I sent you the wrong file.

words.def: To start to do something, or to start happening.
words.note: Say begin to learn or begin learning, not begin learn. In daily talk start is more common; begin is a bit more formal.

ex.en: The movie *begins* at eight.
Let's *begin* with the first question.

col.en: The meeting *begins* with a short presentation.
I *began* to learn English two years ago.
To *begin* with, I don't have enough time.
What time does it *begin*? I don't want to be late.

words.def: Not inside a building or place.
words.note: Say I'm outside, not I'm in outside or I'm at outside. In Darija we say فبرا, but English doesn't need a preposition before outside.

ex.en: The kids are playing *outside*.
I'll wait for you *outside*.

col.en: Let's go *outside*, it's a nice day.
Someone is waiting for you *outside* the building.
I don't check my emails *outside* office hours.
It's cold *outside*, so take a jacket.

texts.title: Text 1 – Moving day
texts.en:
Last Saturday, my cousin Yassine *moved|move* to a new apartment in Rabat. He asked me to help, so I *brought|bring* a friend along.

When we arrived, a lot of *people|people* were standing *outside|outside* the building. *Almost|almost* everyone from his family was there. We *began|begin* with the heavy things, like the fridge and the sofa. Then I *made a mistake|make a mistake*: I put the kitchen boxes in the bedroom. Yassine just laughed and said it was fine.

By the afternoon, we were *behind|behind* schedule, so we ordered pizza. While we were eating, Yassine *found|find* out that his new neighbor is from my city. In the end, we all *had fun|have fun* playing cards on the floor. I *almost|almost* always say yes when a friend needs help.

texts.title: Text 2 – A day at the call center
texts.en:
To *begin|begin* with, I work in a call center. Most *people|people* think it's easy, but it isn't. Many customers *find|find* it hard to explain their problem on the phone.

Sometimes I *make mistakes|make a mistake* too, and I say, "Sorry, my mistake!" When a problem is big, I *bring|bring* it up with my manager. I don't want to fall *behind|behind* with my tasks, but I also need a break. At lunch, I go *outside|outside* for some fresh air. It's cold *outside|outside* today, so I only stay five minutes.

After the break, I *move|move* on to the next task. At five o'clock, I'm *almost|almost* ready to go home, but one more customer calls. I like my team, and we *have fun|have fun* together even on busy days.
